title: Learning Reliable and Intuitive Temporal Logic Rules for Interpretable Time Series Classification

problem.claim: Safety-critical time series classification requires interpretable rules that provide explicit and rigorous rationales.

gap.claim: Existing rule-based methods can produce rules inconsistent with the model's actual decisions and independently weight time points rather than modeling consecutive temporal properties.

contributions.claim: A neuro-symbolic model named TemporalRule automatically learns Signal Temporal Logic rules for interpretable time series classification.
Gradient grafting directly optimizes neural networks representing discrete rules so the learned rules can determine classification results.
A temporal logical layer simulates Until, EA, and AE operators by adaptively learning the time bounds of involved intervals.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe TemporalRule as a novel neuro-symbolic model.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On diverse real-world datasets in safety-critical domains, the authors report superior and stable classification accuracy relative to state-of-the-art rule-based approaches.
The authors report that the learned rules precisely and concisely explain classification results, producing a trustable model.

narrative_sequence.summary: Rule-based time series classifiers are used in safety-critical scenarios because they offer explicit rationales.
Discrete rules may not match continuous neural decision processes, and independently weighted time points do not reflect consecutive temporal properties.
TemporalRule learns Signal Temporal Logic rules using gradient grafting and a temporal logical layer with adaptive interval bounds.
The temporal operators create consistent weights for consecutive time points.
Experiments on real-world safety-critical datasets are reported to show strong accuracy and concise explanations.
